1.explanation: The only part of the Smalltalk language definition responsible for matching string literals is the “string” property in prism-smalltalk.js. Its regular expression is /'(?:''|[^'])+'/, which requires at least one repetition of either a doubled quote ('') or any non-quote character between the delimiters. That means an empty string literal (no content between the quotes) will not match, so '' isn’t treated as a string. Changing the + to * (zero or more) would allow matching empty content and fix the highlighting of empty strings.
1.bug_scenario: In the Prism demo screenshot the empty Smalltalk string literal ('') in the code “anObject withEmptyString: ''  shouldNotBeGreenHere: 'shouldBeGreenHere'” is not recognized as a string and is not highlighted in green. In contrast, Rouge handles it correctly (it shows the empty string in green), so Prism’s Smalltalk grammar is failing to match zero‐length string content.

2.explanation: The core of the bug lies in the definition of the 'string' pattern within Prism.languages.smalltalk. Currently it is defined as /'(?:''|[^'])+'/ which requires at least one character (either a doubled quote '' or any non-quote) inside the delimiters. An empty string ('') contains no interior characters, so it fails to match. Changing the + quantifier to * (zero or more) in both prism-smalltalk.js and its minified version will allow '' to be recognized and highlighted correctly.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots show that an empty Smalltalk string literal ('') is not being recognized or highlighted as a string by Prism. In the first image (Prism demo), the '' appears uncolored and adjacent tokens are mis-classified, whereas in the second image (Rouge demo), the empty string '' is correctly highlighted in green as a string.
